posts.altText: Five-frame text carousel about finding project information. It recommends a message board for updates, tasks with deadlines, and grouped project files, then introduces Basecamp as one shared project home.
posts.caption:
Scattered information creates its own work: finding the update, tracking down the file, checking the deadline.

A shared project home gives each kind of information a clear place. The habit matters too: new updates belong with the project, not just in someone’s inbox.
posts.emotion: Inferred: frustration with constant searching and a desire to feel organized and in control.

frames.body:
A project needs a shared home—not another tab to check.
Start with these three essentials.
frames.heading: Still hunting for the project update?

frames.body: Keep project updates on a message board, so the team has a clear place to look for context.
frames.heading: Give decisions a place to live

frames.body:
Keep tasks and deadlines in the project.
Make it clear what needs doing and when it’s due.
frames.heading: Make the next step easy to find

frames.body: Group project assets and proofs together, so people know where to look before asking around.
frames.heading: Keep the files with the work

posts.altText: Single text-led note headed “Same project. Different expectations?” It lists five items for a useful project note: who, why, how, expectations, and deliverables. It ends with “Try Basecamp free.”
posts.caption:
A task list explains what needs doing. A project note adds the context behind it.

Who is involved? Why does the work matter? How will it happen? What does everyone expect—and what will be delivered?

Keeping those answers together gives the team something concrete to refer back to when questions come up.
posts.emotion: Inferred: unease about misunderstandings and a desire for shared clarity before work moves forward.
